name: CombinePolygons
formula: =LAMBDA(verticesArrText,[count],LET(i, IF(ISOMITTED(count), 1, count), n, ROWS(verticesArrText), cVerticesText, INDEX(verticesArrText, i, 1), otherVertices, {ref}RemoveRow(verticesArrText, i), verticesArrText_updated, {ref}Loop_CombinePolygons(cVerticesText, otherVertices), isCombined, ROWS(verticesArrText_updated) < n, output, IF(OR(i = n, ROWS(verticesArrText_updated) = 1), verticesArrText_updated, IF(isCombined, {ref}CombinePolygons(verticesArrText_updated, 1), {ref}CombinePolygons(verticesArrText, i + 1))), output))
comment: Combines a column of polygons into as few outlines as their overlaps allow. verticesArrText is a column of strict ARRAYTOTEXT strings, each an n×2 list of (x, y) rows. count is optional and is the 1-based polygon to try next; omit it to start at 1. Overlapping polygons become one union string. Separate polygons stay on their own rows. A string shorter than 2 characters returns #VALUE!. Last Update at 2026-11-03.
